meta.title: Detective — a cosy mystery without ads
meta.description: Look over the room, find the evidence, name the one who did it. No ads, no accounts, no tracking; works offline.

home.searchHow: “Just searching” is a room without suspects: things in new places every time.

intro.medium: Medium level: one of the leads may turn out to be false.
intro.hard: Hard level: the innocent tell the truth, and only the one who did it lies.

search.tip: Scroll the room and touch the things from the list.
search.room: The room. Touch the things from the list.
search.keys: Arrow keys move the pointer, Enter touches, plus and minus change the size.

suspects.title: Who did it?
suspects.lead: Each piece of evidence points at a trait. Only one person has them all.
suspects.wrong: No, it is not {name}: “{clue}” does not fit.
suspects.stepsTitle: How to find who did it
suspects.medium1: Tap a person: the card shows their traits and what is known about them.
suspects.medium2: Find what does not fit them, for example: no key, though the door was opened with a key; an alibi for the moment it happened; evidence that is not theirs (a dark hair, but their hair is fair).
suspects.medium3: Tap “Set aside” and pick that reason. The one left last did it.
suspects.mediumNote: Careful: one piece of evidence may be a false lead — a daytime visitor could have left it. It rules nobody out.
suspects.hard1: Tap a person: the card shows their traits, what is known about them and what they say.
suspects.hard2: The innocent tell the truth; only the one who did it lies. A person is set aside by evidence that does not fit them, by someone else’s statement that gives them an alibi, or by two statements that cannot both be true — then it is one of those two.
suspects.hard3: Tap “Set aside”, pick one reason or two, and “Check”. The one left last did it.
suspects.hardNote: A person’s own statement proves nothing. Neither the evidence alone nor the statements alone are enough.
suspects.rule: To name the one who did it, set the others aside — with a reason for each.
suspects.last: One person is left. Open the card and name them.
suspects.pick: Pick one reason, or two that prove it together.

facts.key: Has a key to the door
facts.noKey: Has no key to the door

away.mailSorting: sorting mail at the post office

locked.name: The lock is whole
locked.text: The door was opened with a key: the one who did it has a key.

time.name: The pocket watch stopped at {time}
time.text: That is when it happened. Whoever has an alibi for that time did not do it.

rulings.locked: Set aside: {name}. No key, and the door was opened with a key.
rulings.time: Set aside: {name}. At {time} — {where}: that is an alibi.
rulings.clue: Set aside: {name}. “{clue}” does not fit their traits.
rulings.hasKey: Not set aside: {name} has a key, so this circumstance does not rule them out.
rulings.free: Not set aside: {name} has no alibi for {time}.
rulings.fits: Not set aside: “{clue}” fits the traits of {name}.
rulings.visitor: Not set aside: “{clue}” is a false lead — a daytime visitor ({visitor}) could have left it. It rules nobody out.
rulings.vouched: Set aside: {name}. The statement of {speaker} gives an alibi: if {name} had done it, that statement would be true.
rulings.clash: Set aside: {name}. The statements of {a} and {b} cannot both be true. Only the one who did it lies, so it is one of those two.
rulings.own: Not set aside: the own statement of {name} proves nothing — the one who did it lies.
rulings.possible: Not set aside: all of this can be true even if {name} did it.

result.comeBack: Come back tomorrow for a new case.
result.falseLead: False lead — “{clue}”: {visitor} left it by day ({why}).
result.left: Everybody else is ruled out — {name} is left.

lostLetter.title: The Lost Letter
lostLetter.text: In the morning a sealed letter lay on the detective’s desk. By noon it was gone. Nobody forced the door — so the visitor was someone who belongs here.
lostLetter.ending: {name} admits it: the letter came to her by mistake, and she put it on the desk herself. Then she doubted the address and took it back. The letter is with the detective again.

midnightCall.title: A Call at Midnight
midnightCall.text: At midnight the telephone rang in the study. Silence on the line. And on the desk — an unsigned note: “Tomorrow at seven. Do not be late.” Wet footprints lead from the door.
midnightCall.ending: {name} laughs: the note is hers — an invitation to her first concert. She forgot to sign it, and she rang to check whether the detective was still awake.

dailySeal.title: The Missing Seal
dailySeal.text: The detective’s seal is gone from the desk. The lock is whole, the window shut. One of the acquaintances came by while the owner was out.
dailySeal.ending: The answer is simple: {name} took the seal to stamp a greeting card. The seal is back in its place.

dailyVase.title: The Broken Vase
dailyVase.text: Someone broke a vase in the study and quietly swept up the pieces. But traces remain.
dailyVase.ending: {name} does not deny it: the vase fell by accident, and a new one just like it is already ordered.

dailyNote.title: A Note in the Drawer
dailyNote.text: An unsigned note turned up in the desk drawer: “Thank you for everything.” Who put it there?
dailyNote.ending: {name} smiles: it is thanks for an old favour. The signature just did not fit.

dailyBiscuits.title: The Empty Biscuit Tin
dailyBiscuits.text: The biscuit tin on the shelf was emptied in a single day. Crumbs lead to the door.
dailyBiscuits.ending: {name} blushes and promises to bake new biscuits — twice as many.

fairPie.title: A Pie for the Fair
fairPie.text: Today is the fair, and Emma’s apple pie was to go to the contest. At dawn it stood on its stand by the window — now there are only crumbs. Ginger the cat pretends to be asleep.
fairPie.ending: {name} looks at his shoes: he feared the pie would be late, so at dawn he took it to the fair himself. It is on the judges’ table already — wearing the winner’s blue ribbon. Ginger had nothing to do with it.

nightShift.title: The Night Shift
nightShift.text: At night the watchman noticed: the bakery door stood ajar, the lamps over the counter were burning. Floury footprints cross the floor. Somebody has lost a glove and a key.
nightShift.ending: {name} sighs: so much for the surprise. She came at night to bake a cake for the watchman’s birthday — and hurried home so fast that she lost her key and a glove. The cake is ready; it will just be given a day early.

bakeryRecipe.title: The Missing Recipe
bakeryRecipe.text: The notebook with the recipe of the bakery’s plaited loaf is gone from the drawer under the counter. The lock is whole — so it was someone who belongs here.
bakeryRecipe.ending: {name} hands the notebook back: the recipe only needed copying, to bake the loaf at home for a holiday.

bakeryBun.title: The Bitten Bun
bakeryBun.text: In the basket on the windowsill lies a bun with a bite taken out of it — and put back. Who was in such a hurry?
bakeryBun.ending: {name} blushes and pays for the whole basket of buns — enough for everybody.

bakerySign.title: The Sign Upside Down
bakerySign.text: In the morning the pretzel sign hung on the door upside down. Somebody put it up again while the bakery was closed.
bakerySign.ending: {name} laughs: a draught blew the sign down, and it had to be hung back in the dark, by touch.

bakeryJam.title: The Empty Shelf
bakeryJam.text: A jar of raspberry jam is gone from the shelf. In its place lie a coin and an unsigned note: “Badly needed.”
bakeryJam.ending: {name} explains: the till was closed, and the jam was needed for tea at once. The coin is the payment — with a tip.

strangeSuitcase.title: The Wrong Suitcase
strangeSuitcase.text: Two suitcases just alike lie in the waiting hall. One has just been opened — and the things inside belong to somebody else. Someone took the wrong one, then put it back in the wrong place. By chance or on purpose?
strangeSuitcase.ending: {name} clutches her head: hurrying for the train, she grabbed the wrong suitcase and noticed only on the platform — sheet music inside instead of her camera. She quietly put it back. Now each suitcase is with its owner.

lastTrain.title: The Last Train
lastTrain.text: The last train has gone. An open case is left in the waiting hall — and there is no violin in it. The musician stepped away for a minute, only to look at the timetable.
lastTrain.ending: {name} spreads his hands: the violin lay in the draught by the door, so he locked it in his little room — away from the damp and from strangers. He has the key, the violin is whole, and the musician is already playing a thank-you.

recipeBook.title: The Recipe Book
recipeBook.text: At night the book of recipes vanished from the bakery. The door stands ajar, but the lock is whole — it was opened with a key. Floury footprints cross the floor.
recipeBook.ending: {name} owns up: the binding of the recipe book had come apart, so he quietly took it to the bookbinder — to bring it back in a new cover for the bakery’s anniversary. The book is on its shelf again, as good as new.

missingStamp.title: The Missing Stamp
missingStamp.text: In the evening a rare stamp vanished from the album on the detective’s desk. The pocket watch beside it has stopped — somebody must have knocked it in a hurry. Each of the six has told where they were at that minute.
missingStamp.ending: {name} owns up: he took the stamp to have it framed in secret — a present for the detective on the agency’s anniversary. The library was made up, so as not to spoil the surprise. The stamp is in its frame now, on the wall.

says.anna: At {time} I was at home, alone. Nobody can confirm it.
says.sofia: At {time} I was at the theater, rehearsing.
says.ilona: At {time} I was in the library, at the desk. Nora was in the reading room. And Tamas did not come in today.
says.tamas: At {time} I was in the library — reading next to Nora.
says.nora: At {time} I was in the library, picking photos for an exhibition.
says.viktor: At {time} I was in the café, having tea after my shift.

stationUmbrella.title: Somebody Else’s Umbrella
stationUmbrella.text: Somebody left the waiting hall with another person’s umbrella — and left a broken one under the bench.
stationUmbrella.ending: {name} brings the umbrella back with an apology: both are black, and it was dark outside.

stationClock.title: The Clock Runs Late
stationClock.text: The station clock suddenly fell ten minutes behind, and several passengers nearly missed their trains. Somebody has touched the hands.
stationClock.ending: {name} explains: the clock had stopped, and the hands had to be set by guesswork. The clockmaker has been sent for.

stationBouquet.title: A Bouquet without a Note
stationBouquet.text: A bouquet lies on the ledge of the ticket window, with no note. The clerk says somebody put it down and ran.
stationBouquet.ending: {name} blushes: the bouquet is thanks for a wallet that was found and given back.

stationTimetable.title: One Line Too Many
stationTimetable.text: A line has appeared in the timetable that was not there yesterday: a train to the sea at twenty-five o’clock. Who wrote it?
stationTimetable.ending: {name} laughs: it is a joke for a nephew who has just learnt to read the timetable. The line is already wiped off.

wrongParcel.title: Somebody Else’s Parcel
wrongParcel.text: Mrs Vera was waiting for a parcel with a new pendulum for her clock. In the morning it lay on the counter, in brown paper tied with string. Now another parcel lies in its place — just the same to look at, but lighter.
wrongParcel.ending: {name} looks into his bag and blushes: the same paper, the same string — he took somebody else’s parcel instead of his own. The pendulum goes back to Mrs Vera, and with it a box of chocolates for the trouble.

nightLetter.title: The Letter That Could Not Wait
nightLetter.text: At night somebody lit the lamp over the counter in the closed post office — damp footprints lead to it from the door. In the morning a letter is gone from the “To be sent” box, and a lost key lies on the mat by the door.
nightLetter.ending: {name} confesses: in the evening she wrote her sister an angry letter in a temper — and could not sleep all night. She has a key to the post office: she looks after the flowers here. She took that letter back, and a new, kind one will be the first to go.

postPostcard.title: The Lighthouse Postcard
postPostcard.text: For years a postcard with a lighthouse hung on the post office wall — sent long ago by a traveller who went round the world. Today only a drawing pin is left in its place.
postPostcard.ending: {name} shows a sketchbook: the postcard was borrowed for an evening to draw the lighthouse for a granddaughter who dreams of the sea. Now the postcard is back on the wall.

postHorn.title: The Brass Horn
postHorn.text: A brass post horn has always hung above the post counter. This morning the hook is empty.
postHorn.ending: {name} brings the horn back, polished till it shines: it will be blown at the town festival, and it ought to gleam.

postPen.title: The Pen on a Chain
postPen.text: On the customers’ desk the pen is always chained down — and still it is gone. The chain is broken.
postPen.ending: {name} looks embarrassed: the letter was long, the pen was comfortable, and the chain was old. A new chain has already been bought.

postWeights.title: The Missing Weights
postWeights.text: A little box of weights always stands beside the post office scales. Today it is empty, and there is no way to weigh the parcels.
postWeights.ending: {name} brings the weights back: they were borrowed to weigh flour for a pie for the postman — it is his birthday today.

anniversaryCake.title: The Anniversary Cake
anniversaryCake.text: The café is twenty years old today! The festive cake with a cream rose waited for the guests in the glass case — and now only crumbs lie in its place. The party starts in two hours.
anniversaryCake.ending: {name} spreads her hands: she took the cake to her own kitchen to pipe a cream “20” on it — and had no time to tell anyone. The cake is on its way back, even lovelier than before.

midnightWaltz.title: The Midnight Waltz
midnightWaltz.text: At midnight the neighbours heard somebody playing a waltz in the closed café. Now all is quiet, the wall lamps by the piano are lit, and music lies open on the stand. Who was playing here in the middle of the night?
midnightWaltz.ending: {name} smiles sheepishly: he has been learning the piano in secret for a long time, and the café’s key was left with him in case of trouble. On his night round he could not resist — the waltz was meant for the café’s anniversary. Now the owner asks him to play it at the party.

cafeCup.title: The Swallow Cup
cafeCup.text: The café’s oldest cup is gone from the shelf — the one with a painted swallow. The very first owner drank her coffee from it.
cafeCup.ending: {name} explains: a little crack had appeared on the cup, so it was taken to be mended. In a week the swallow will be back on its shelf — with a thin line of gold where the crack was.

cafeCrossword.title: The Unfinished Crossword
cafeCrossword.text: Every morning a fresh newspaper lies on the counter, and the regulars solve the crossword together. Today the newspaper is gone — together with the last, hardest word.
cafeCrossword.ending: {name} brings the newspaper back, laughing: the crossword would not let go, so it was finished at home. The last word is “swallow”.

cafeSpoon.title: The Silver Spoon
cafeSpoon.text: Every slice of honey cake here comes with a silver spoon. In the evening the spoons are counted — one is missing.
cafeSpoon.ending: {name} finds the spoon in a coat pocket and blushes: in the middle of a good conversation it slipped in there instead of a handkerchief. Now the spoon is back in its place.

cafeGuestbook.title: The Guest Book
cafeGuestbook.text: The thick guest book that always lies on the counter by the till is gone. For twenty years guests have written their wishes in it.
cafeGuestbook.ending: {name} brings the book back: the warmest wishes in it were copied out for a grandmother who once met her husband here. The book is back on the counter.

about.title: About
about.text: A cosy mystery without ads, accounts or tracking. Everything stays on this device. Works offline.
about.how: Find every thing from the list in the room — some of them are evidence. Then open the people’s cards: each piece of evidence points at a trait, and only one person has them all.
about.keys: Keyboard: arrows move the pointer over the room (faster with Shift), Enter touches, + and − change the size.
